ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a schematic bar chart of the day-arc lengths of three places; the vertical axis is labeled day-arc radian (°), with scale marks of 140, 162.5, 180, and 220. The three bars correspond respectively to ①, ②, and Beijing: the day arc of ① is about 162.5°, the day arc of ② is 140°, and the day arc of Beijing is 220°. Reasoning: On the same day, the day arcs of places at the same latitude in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres are complementary, that is, the sum of the day arcs is 360°. Beijing's day arc is 220°, and its complementary day arc is 360°－220°＝140°, exactly equal to the day arc of ②, so ② and Beijing have the same latitude value, and their latitude levels are equal. The day arc of ① is 162.5°, and its complementary value is 360°－162.5°＝197.5°, which is less than Beijing's 220°; on this day, in the Northern Hemisphere, the higher the latitude, the longer the day arc, so the latitude corresponding to ① is lower than Beijing, and also lower than ②, which is at the same latitude as Beijing. Therefore the latitude-level relationship is ①＜②＝Beijing.
